notes.title: Basic Concept of Bar Graph
notes.content: A Bar Graph represents data using rectangular bars. The height or length of each bar shows the value of a category. The horizontal line (X-axis) shows categories and the vertical line (Y-axis) shows numbers. Example: Sales of different months.

notes.title: Understanding Axis and Scale
notes.content: Always check the scale carefully. For example, 1 unit may represent 10 students or ₹1000. If you misread the scale, the entire answer will be wrong. First read the title, then check both axes.

notes.title: How to Compare Bars
notes.content: To compare two bars, look at their heights. The taller bar means a higher value. To find the difference, subtract the smaller value from the larger value.

notes.title: Important Formulas
notes.content: Difference = Larger value minus Smaller value. Percentage = (Part / Total) multiplied by 100. Average = Sum of all values divided by Number of values.

notes.title: Common Mistakes
notes.content: Ignoring the scale. Reading the wrong category or year. Guessing without calculation. Ignoring units like ₹, numbers, or percentage.

notes.title: Quick Summary
notes.content: Read the title first. Check the scale. Observe the data carefully. Then perform calculations step by step. Avoid rushing.

tricks.title: Quick Difference Method
tricks.explanation: If numbers are close, think how much needs to be added to reach the bigger number instead of full subtraction.

tricks.title: Fast Percentage Trick
tricks.explanation: Find 10% first, then multiply as needed.

tricks.title: Average Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If numbers are evenly spaced, the middle number is the average.

tricks.title: Double Bar Strategy
tricks.explanation: Complete one category fully before comparing with another to avoid confusion.
tricks.example: Write 2019 and 2020 sales separately before comparing.

tricks.title: Quick Ratio Simplification
tricks.explanation: Divide both numbers by a common factor.

tricks.title: Fast Addition Trick
tricks.explanation: Round numbers to make addition easier.

tricks.title: Identify Highest and Lowest Quickly
tricks.explanation: First find the tallest and shortest bars before deeper comparison.
tricks.example: If one bar is 900 and others are between 500 and 700, 900 is highest.

tricks.title: Approximation Method
tricks.explanation: If answer options are far apart, use estimation instead of exact calculation.
tricks.example: If result is around 880 and options are 200, 500, 900, choose 900.
